thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed in control-plane public API (org-lookup / auth). Rolling paging to oncall team. Threshold breached: 5xx > 2% sustained for 7m. Metrics: https://internal.metrics/redwood/controlplane/5xx :rotating_light:

mira (oncall): I'm on it. Pulling graphs now. Can someone confirm scope — is this affecting hosted API and Dedicated control-plane calls?

alex (sre): Seeing spike across regions us-east-1 and eu-west-1, mostly HTTP 502/504 from config-service and auth-proxy. Traces show increased latencies to auth-db pool ~1.2s -> 6s.

jordan (control-plane): We're seeing org-lookup timeouts bubbled to the gateway. Query fanout increased by 3x around 17:40 UTC. Suspect recent rollout to org-cache v2?

shaun (auth-team): We're getting high connection churn on the auth cluster, DB errors show 'too many clients'. Rolling up a quick connection pool bump now and enabling emergency read-replicas.

emily (pager): Noted. Opening customer-impact tracker. Initial findings: ~4.3% failed calls for API key flows, some users reporting 502 on token verify.

mira (oncall): Mitigation plan for now: 1) Temporarily reduce fanout on org-lookup from 8 -> 3 (gateway config). 2) Enable retry-with-backoff for auth proxy (short window). 3) Throttle non-critical background config refresh endpoints. Can control-plane team make the routing change?

jordan (control-plane): I'll patch gateway policy now. Applying canary to us-east-1 first. Command: `kubectl apply -f gateway-reduce-fanout.yaml --context=us-east-1-cluster`

ops-bot: deploy started by jordan. ci/build/3456 -> gateway-fanout-reduce v2026.3. Canaries: 10% traffic

alex (sre): Observability note: enable debug logs for org-cache misses for 10m to confirm fewer backend hits.

shaun (auth-team): Read-replica enable done. Connection pool increased to 200. Rolling restart auth-proxy pods slowly to recycle stale pools.

emily (pager): Customer-impact update: Affected endpoints: /v1/auth/verify, /v1/org/* (lookup). Top customers experiencing errors: 3 enterprise tenants — tagged and alerted. No billing disruption detected yet.

mira (oncall): After first canary, 5xx rate dropped from 3.8% -> 1.1% in canary region. Rolling to 30% and will monitor 2 min windows.

jordan (control-plane): Rolling to 30% done.

ops-bot: deploy progressed to 30% -> metrics show error decrease: Grafana: https://internal.metrics/redwood/controlplane/5xx?range=30m (canary trace)

alex (sre): We should also add temporary fallback policy: if org-lookup fails after 2 retries, return stale cached org metadata (last known) for product-tier customers to reduce user-facing errors. Implementing a short-lived patch on gateway.

jordan (control-plane): Patch in progress, applying `gateway-fallback-stale-org.patch` as emergency flag.

shaun (auth-team): After pool bump and replica, auth latencies normalized from 6s -> 0.8s. Logs show the DB got backpressure early; we need long-term fix but this stabilizes immediate failures.

emily (pager): Customer-impact update: error rate across hosted API down to ~0.9% global; Dedicated control-plane tenants saw similar improvement after routing changes. Marking incident severity decreased to S2.

mira (oncall): Passing to next oncall for monitoring and post-incident actions. Summary for handoff: root: auth DB connection exhaustion + increased org-lookup fanout after org-cache rollout; symptom: 5xx + timeouts at gateway. Immediate mitigations: increased auth pool, enabled read-replicas, reduced fanout, deployed stale-org fallback, throttled non-critical refreshes.

emily (pager): Adding timeline and customer notes to incident tracker: https://incidents.local/RED-1798601234

alex (sre): Quick notes for follow-up: - Investigate org-cache v2 rollout config that increased concurrent fanout. Possible bug in cache warm-up logic. - Add circuit breaker on gateway org-lookup path. - Hard quota on org-lookup concurrency per request. - DB sizing / connection pooling review for auth cluster.

shaun (auth-team): Agree. Also recommend adding a slow-start for read-replica warm-up and autoscaling on auth proxies.

jordan (control-plane): I'll open a PR to revert the aggressive fanout default and add feature flag gating.

emily (pager): Assigning postmortem lead: alex (sre). Owner for control-plane changes: jordan. Auth follow-up owner: shaun. Target: preliminary postmortem in 48h.

mira (oncall): Handoff complete. I'll stay available for 30m in case errors spike again. Good job all. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity changed S1 -> S2. Incident acknowledged by oncall. Current status: stabilizing.

emily (pager): Closing note: please add any additional observations here (stack traces, correlating deploys, customer reports). We'll merge into the timeline for the postmortem.
